title: Organizing transitions and their cascades: Generalized symmetry enforcement in massless flows or Higgs transitions
abstract: We study the role of generalized symmetry in massless renormalization group flows or Higgs transitions. In particular, we revisit the massless renormalization group flows in unitary minimal models, $\mathbf{M}(p,p+1) \rightarrow \overline{\mathbf{M}(p-1,p)}$ preserving the fusion ring symmetry $\text{FR} (SU(2)_{p-2})\subset \mathbf{M}(p,p+1)$ where $p$ is an integer satisfying $p>3$. In this series of flows, we demonstrate that the unbroken fusion ring symmetry $\text{FR} (SU(2)_{p-2})$ eliminates all relevant perturbations in the $\overline{\mathbf{M}(p-1,p)}$ model. Hence, the infrared theory $\overline{\mathbf{M}(p-1,p)}$ is stable at the level of the scaling analysis and can be interpreted as a (weak-)symmetry-enforced gapless phase in contemporary theoretical physics. Phenomenologically, by the folding trick, the unbroken fusion ring symmetry corresponds to a (half-)integer spin nonsimple current, a variant of the Cooper pair involving nonabelian anyons generated from the coset or level-rank duality structures. Moreover, we demonstrate that the structure of (half-)integer spin nonsimple current plays a fundamental role in causing the resonance effect of relevant and dangerously irrelevant perturbations. This resonance effect may result in the cascade of phase transitions (or the system flows to unexplored fixed points), and the symmetry can be a stopper of such unconventional flows.
summary: This paper uses advanced CFT techniques to analyze how generalized symmetries stabilize massless Renormalization Group flows between minimal models. It demonstrates that specific unbroken symmetries eliminate dangerous perturbations, confirming the stability of the resulting infrared phase as a gapless state. This work provides a deep connection between abstract algebraic structures and the robustness of physical quantum phases.
main_problem: The study investigates how generalized symmetry dictates the stability of massless Renormalization Group (RG) flows or Higgs transitions between different Conformal Field Theories (CFTs). The core goal is to understand how unbroken symmetries enforce gapless phases during these theoretical phase changes.
main_result: In specific minimal model flows, the presence of an unbroken fusion ring symmetry eliminates all relevant perturbations in the infrared theory, confirming its stability as a (weak-)symmetry-enforced gapless phase. Furthermore, this structure dictates potential cascade effects between different fixed points.
method: The analysis employs Hamiltonian formalism for CFTs and their RG mappings, combining perturbative checks with nonperturbative algebraic methods involving symmetry constraints like fusion rings and coset structures.
model_or_system: The primary system is the massless RG flow between unitary minimal models, specifically $M(p, p+1) ightarrow M(p-1, p)$, which models theoretical phase transitions analogous to Higgs phenomena. The underlying mathematical framework involves CFTs and their associated symmetry algebras.
key_observables: Unbroken fusion ring symmetry $	ext{FR}(SU(2)_{p-2})$, stability of the infrared (IR) fixed point, and the structure of (half-)integer spin nonsimple currents.
important_parameters: The integer parameter $p$ defining the minimal models ($p>3$), and the flow parameters governing relevant/irrelevant perturbations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of RG flows and relies heavily on symmetry arguments to prove stability, contrasting with purely algebraic methods that might not guarantee physical stability.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes key concepts: pairing structure involving nonsimple currents, symmetry-enforced gaplessness, coset/level rank duality structures, and the potential for phase transition cascades.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the RG flow by first establishing the role of generalized symmetry in stabilizing the IR theory. It then details how specific symmetries (like $	ext{FR}(SU(2)_{p-2})$) eliminate relevant perturbations, leading to conclusions about gapless phases and potential cascade dynamics.
why_interesting: The concept of symmetry enforcing stability in RG flows is highly relevant for understanding quantum critical points and topological order in condensed matter systems, providing a powerful theoretical tool beyond standard perturbation theory.
